demonstrates: The media-type retention policy (ADR 0007). A well-behaved Field declines to retain a video attachment excluded by the run's media-type include set, carrying a stable attachment_ref core would project onto the shared skipped_attachments Note property, alongside a retained text attachment on the same record. A second, separate record then shows a hostile Field staging an excluded type anyway, which core rejects as 'artifact.type_excluded' -- distinct from 'artifact.oversized', the other retention-adjacent rejection.
notes: Record 1's decline is well-behaved and its checkpoint commits normally; record 2 is a deliberately hostile record demonstrating what core does when a Field ignores the declared policy and stages an excluded type anyway. Both cases are shown once for review; in the conformance kit each is exercised as its own scenario.

body.text:
# Team standup recording

Hi Joe,

Sharing this week's standup notes and the recording.

Alice

Attachments:
- notes.txt, 40 bytes, retained locally.
- team-standup-recording.mp4, approximately 612 MB, not retained: video is outside the default media-type include set, so it stays at its source.

detail: Core resolves handle 'a0021' inside the staging directory, verifies it is a regular file, and streams it.
Core's own digest matches the declared one and text/plain is included by the run's media-type policy, so the original is installed at its content-addressed path.

video/mp4 is excluded by the run's media-type include set. The Field declined to retain it rather than have core reject a staged copy; core stores no bytes and computes no digest for it. attachment_ref names the declined attachment stably, so core can record it in the Note's skipped_attachments property.

The Note references the retained artifact ID in artifacts/attachments, and the declined attachment's reference in skipped_attachments. Both lists are independent: the retained attachment's presence does not require or preclude anything about the skipped one.
The retained artifact and the Note are both durable, so the cursor advances. Declining an attachment never blocks the checkpoint: it is a policy outcome, not a failure.

body.text:
# Second copy of the recording

A hostile Field stages the same excluded type instead of declining it.

note: video/mp4 is excluded by the run's media-type include set, and this Field staged it anyway instead of declining it. The frame is wire-schema well formed -- a validator checking only the schema has no basis to reject a staged video reference -- so this is caught by the artifact-validation step, before any filesystem call, exactly as the size threshold is: 'artifact.type_excluded', distinct from 'artifact.oversized'.

detail: The declared media type video/mp4 is excluded by the run's media-type retention policy. A well-behaved Field would have declined this attachment as not_retained instead of staging it.
A rejected record fails the run: core stops consuming output and commits no further checkpoint. The checkpoint already committed for record 1 stands, because it was durable before it was committed.
Child terminated and the run's staging directory removed.
